title: NO KINGS! "We the People" Democracy Fair in Palo Alto
description:
This Flag Day, join us for a democracy fair. Following a day of peaceful protests held in counterpoint to Donald Trump’s militaristic charade, we will host a celebration of what makes America truly great—and truly good.

On June 14, we will gather not just in protest, but in defiance—loud, proud, joyful defiance of a tinpot wannabe tyrant who thinks that celebrating his birthday matters more than honoring the flag that symbolizes our freedom. The democracy fair will be an occasion for people to convene after No Kings events being held across the Peninsula.

This event—jointly sponsored by Bend the Arc, Indivisible Mid-Peninsula, Indivisible Palo Alto Plus, Indivisible Portola Valley, and It’s Blue Turn—will celebrate patriotism, not militarism. In saying NO to kings, we will also say YES to democracy.

description:

Instead, there will be costumes, music, and American flags. It will be a procession of your friends and neighbors, in all their democratic glory and all their splendid diversity.

In Washington, D.C., Trump will oversee a military display that echoes the aggressive pretensions of dictators overseas. His self-serving event will shamefully contradict the spirit of the democratic republic for which our flag stands.

In Palo Alto, as elsewhere across the country, Americans will rise up to celebrate our liberation from kingly pretension. We will gather not just in protest, but in defiance—loud, proud, joyful defiance of a tinpot wannabe tyrant who thinks that celebrating his birthday matters more than honoring the flag that symbolizes our freedom.

title: YDG University - Hate and Politics
description:
This six-week virtual course explores the historical and contemporary impact of hate groups and white nationalist militias on American politics and society. From their origins in post-Civil War America to their digital presence today, we will examine how these groups operate, recruit, and influence public discourse. Through historical case studies, data analysis, and counter-organizing strategies, students will develop a critical understanding of hate groups and the tools necessary to challenge their influence, fight misinformation, and combat hate in politics. 


By the end of this course, you will:

-Gain a comprehensive understanding of the origins and evolution of hate groups in America.

-Analyze the role of hate groups in shaping national and state politics, with a specific focus on Georgia.

-Investigate how hate groups use digital platforms to spread narratives and recruit members.

-Develop strategies to counter-organize against hate groups at both community and policy levels.

title: Understanding Vaccines from Chickenpox to Cancer: Building Trust Through Conversation
description:
Panel discussion and educational presentation on how vaccines work **with a *special* focus on how to talk to vaccine-hesitant family members and friends.**

## Panelists
- **Dr. Neil Shah, MD, PhD**: Hematologist and oncologist at UCSF
- **Dr. Dawnell Moody, DO, MPH**: Pediatrician based in the Tri-Valley area
- **Dr. Shelley Facente, PhD, MPH**: Adjunct assistant professor at the Berkeley School of Public Health

## What to expect
This event will feature an educational presentation and an open panel discussion on how vaccines work, with a special focus on communicating effectively with vaccine-hesitant family and friends. We will also highlight cutting-edge research in vaccine development, including advancements aimed at preventing or treating cancer and autoimmune diseases such as type 1 diabetes.

Attendees will gain practical tools and data to help guide respectful, informed conversations about vaccines. Our goal is to equip you with the confidence to share accurate information and address common concerns. The event will include an open forum where community members are encouraged to ask questions to a panel of expert physicians and scientists.

The event will take place on June 28th from 11:00 AM to 12:00 PM (noon) on Zoom. It will begin with a brief 10–15 minute presentation, followed by a panel discussion for the remainder of the hour.

### Neil P. Shah, MD, PhD
Neil P. Shah, MD, PhD, received his BS from the University of California, Berkeley, and his MD and PhD degrees from the UCLA School of Medicine. His postdoctoral research in Charles Sawyers’ lab directly led to the clinical investigation and FDA approval of dasatinib, a transformative therapy for patients with chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). He joined the UCSF faculty in 2006 and is the Edward S. Ageno Distinguished Professor in Hematology/Oncology. He is an internationally known expert in targeted therapy for CML and is Chair of the National Comprehensive Cancer Network Chronic Myeloid Leukemia Guidelines Panel. His laboratory continues to conduct molecular studies of human leukemias and attempts to translate expanding knowledge of the genetics of these diseases toward the development of more effective and better tolerated targeted therapeutics. 

### Dr. Dawnell Moody, DO, MPH
Dr. Dawnell Moody is a board-certified pediatrician who has served as a clinical leader in the Tri-Valley healthcare safety net for the past 10 years. Dr. Moody earned a Doctor of Osteopathy degree from Western University of Health Sciences, a Master of Public Health from the University of Massachusetts at Amherst, and has a faculty appointment as an adjunct clinical assistant professor in the Department of Medicine, Division of Primary Care and Population Health at Stanford University School of Medicine. Dr. Moody is also a graduate of the California Health Care Foundation's healthcare leadership program.  

### Shelley Facente, PhD, MPH 
Shelley Facente, PhD, MPH was trained in sociology at Ithaca College in Ithaca, NY, and subsequently received her Master of Public Health and a PhD in Epidemiology from the University of California, Berkeley. In 2009 she founded Facente Consulting, which has since grown into a firm of 11 people devoted to improving the health of communities most neglected and harmed by current and historical systems. She has consulted for a number of schools and community organizations and associations, to help them complete or upgrade their COVID-19 prevention protocols, and make evidence-based decisions about vaccination, programs, and policies based on the latest scientific knowledge and data.

title: One Community Dialogue: Know Your Rights, Know Your Power

sponsor.name: Louisiana Organization for Refugees and Immigrants

description:
Description:
In a time of uncertainty and fear—when legislation is being used to chip away at our most basic constitutional rights—it’s more important than ever to stay informed, united, and civically engaged.

Join the Louisiana Organization for Refugees and Immigrants (LORI) for our monthly One Community Dialogue series, held every second Friday of the month, where we come together to learn how to safely and effectively be civically engaged and action in our democracy.

We’ll talk about:
• What’s happening at the Louisiana State Capitol and why it matters
• Your rights—what you still have and how to protect them
• The legislative process—how bills become law and how YOU can be part of the conversation
• Step-by-step guidance on showing up, giving testimony, and making your voice heard

You do not need prior experience. These sessions are open, welcoming, and designed to help us all find our role in shaping a better future—especially for immigrant and refugee communities.

Let’s come together as one community, because this is our democracy, and our voices matter.

Dates: Every second Friday of the month
Location: Zoom (link will be sent after you sign up) 
Time: 5:30PM -6:30PM

Before the government can detain people pretrial, state and federal law require that pretrial defendants have an evidentiary hearing with the assistance of defense counsel. Hamilton County deprives many pretrial defendants of these rights.

Court Watch is essential in our campaign to end these unconstitutional bail practices.

Our goal is to identify cases where judges set pretrial restrictions like bond. Since magistrate hearings are not public, we observe General Sessions Court during defendants' first appearances. Join Basic Rights Oregon (BRO) at Philomath Pride 2025!
